newsitem.title: UK: Slovak crown seen rising against Czech crown - DMG. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Slovak crown seen rising against Czech crown - DMG. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]

text.p: The Slovak crown is likely to appreciate against the Czech crown and switching into it offers attractive returns, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said on Thursday.

"We...expect the Slovak crown to strengthen against the Czech crown over the next two months. The current spike in Slovak interest rates make a long Slovak crown position funded in Czech crowns attractive," it said in a strategy report.

"In addition this trade offers some protection against the devaluation risk associated with investing in eastern Europe as the close trade links between the Czeck and Slovak Republics make the devaluation of one currency without (corrects from "with" to "without") the concurrent devaluation of the other unlikely," it said.
It noted the Czech crown currently trades at a five percent premium against the level implied by its basket, while the Slovak currency trades around par.
One month funding in Czech crowns is currently available at 12.5 percent whereas one month offshore deposit rates in Slovak crows are around 19 percent.
"Thus investors can lock into an interest rate carry of approximately 6.5 percent," it added.
